body:
Should we clarify in [11.3.2](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x20-V11-Cryptography.md#v113-encryption-algorithms)
from
> Verify that only secure, authenticated **ciphers and modes** such as AES with GCM are used.

to
> Verify that only secure, authenticated **ciphers and their modes** such as AES with GCM are used.

?

comments.body: I think that is a very nice clarification here. I like it! 🙏🏼
@randomstuff - if there is an agreement we can PR it in

The question also applies to 11.6.1?
> 11.6.1 Verify that only approved cryptographic algorithms and modes of operation are used for key generation and seeding, and digital signature generation and verification.

@elarlang, yes. In 11.6.1 we have the same case. Thank you for mentioning it. 
And suggest clarify "ciphers or **their** modes " in 11.2.2 also.

I find that the difference between 11.3.2 and 11.3.3 is not clear.

| # | Description | Level | #v5.0.be |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **11.3.2** | Verify that only secure, authenticated ciphers and modes such as AES with GCM are used. | 1 | v5.0.be-6.5.2 |
| **11.3.3** | Verify that encrypted data is protected against unauthorized modification preferably by using an approved authenticated encryption method or by combining an approved encryption method with an approved MAC algorithm. | 2 | v5.0.be-6.5.4 |

11.3.3 is "you shall use authenticated encryption".

Therefore, 11.3.2 is not supposed to be "you shall use authenticated encryption" but only "you shall use approved cryptographic mechanisms" but it kind-of says "you shall use authenticated encryption".

@elarlang , @randomstuff colleagues, let me share my thoughts and sum-up of topics raised above:

1.  Support changing 11.3.2 to "Verify that only **approved** ciphers and **their** modes such as AES with GCM are used." Comment here: fits as L1 requirement that approved (but it can be that not-authenticated with "build-in MAC") algorithm with strong modes must be be used. And state on "approved **authenticated** algorithm" usage only in 11.3.2 (L2) requirement. And do we needed requirement 11.3.1 after such change, if seems it will be covered by 11.3.2?
2.  Make clarification in 11.6.1 "approved cryptographic algorithms and **their** modes"
3.  Make clarification in 11.2.2  "ciphers or **their** modes"

One more topic related to use of approved cryptographic algorithms for L2 (if you wanted -- can open separate issue for this topic).
In Appendix V "Cryptography" the approved KEX Schemes described (the same as we have for approved hash functions and algorithms there).
So, should we change in 11.6.2 (Section V11.6 Public Key Cryptography)?
from:
>"Verify that **industry-proven cryptographic algorithms** are used for key exchange (such as Diffie-Hellman) with a focus on ensuring that key exchange mechanisms use secure parameters. This will prevent attacks on the key establishment process which could lead to adversary-in-the-middle attacks or cryptographic breaks."

to 
>"Verify that **approved cryptographic algorithms** are used for key exchange (such as Diffie-Hellman) with a focus on ensuring that key exchange mechanisms use secure parameters. This will prevent attacks on the key establishment process which could lead to adversary-in-the-middle attacks or cryptographic breaks."

Yes, I agree that the intent should probably to say "approved" in 11.3.2 and 11.6.2 (and align with 11.6.1).

***

I am not so sure about the "ciphers or **their** modes". For 11.3.2 I would say:

>  Verify that only approved ciphers, modes and authenticated encryption algorithms are used.

The "you must use authenticated encryption" is already the crux of 11.3.3 so it does not need to be in 11.3.2?

As we have "you must use authenticated encryption" in 11.3.3, I would relax 11.3.2 and make clear difference between 11.3.3. and 11.3.2. And aligned with Note in Appendix V Cryptography that "All encrypted messages must be authenticated. ..."
Regarding "their", yes we can align wording with what we have in 4.0.3 ASVS version and put in compact way as "ciphers, modes"
Shall we put 11.3.2 as?: 
> Verify that only approved ciphers, modes are used.

The same for 11.6.1
> Verify that only approved cryptographic **algorithms, modes** of operation are used for key generation and seeding, and digital signature generation and verification.

And 11.2.2
> Verify that the application is designed with crypto agility such that random number, authenticated encryption, MAC, or hashing algorithms, key lengths, rounds, **ciphers, modes** can be reconfigured, upgraded, or swapped at any time, to protect against cryptographic breaks. Similarly, it must also be possible to replace keys and passwords and re-encrypt data. This will allow for seamless upgrades to post-quantum cryptography (PQC), once high-assurance implementations of approved PQC schemes or standards are widely available.
@randomstuff @oleksiidov - please find the solution that satisfies both and PR it in.

@randomstuff, I have reviewed previous posts, and summed up below that we have as a result. 
Shall we go with such changes?:

For [11.3.2](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x20-V11-Cryptography.md#v113-encryption-algorithms) make clear difference from [11.3.3](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x20-V11-Cryptography.md#v113-encryption-algorithms) and state that for 11.3.2 (level L1) the requirement is to use approved (but it can be not-authenticated) algorithm, modes. And leave requirement on "approved authenticated algorithm" only for 11.3.3 (level L2).  Also align wording with what we have in ASVS 4.0.3 version and put "ciphers and modes" as in ASVS 4.0.3:  "ciphers, modes".
So make following changes in 11.3.2 from
> Verify that only **secure, authenticated ciphers and modes** such as AES with GCM are used.

to
> Verify that only **approved ciphers, modes** are used.

*****
In a similar way, for [11.6.1](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x20-V11-Cryptography.md#v116-public-key-cryptography) clarify from "ciphers and modes" to "ciphers, modes".
and change from
> Verify that only approved cryptographic **algorithms and modes** of operation are used for key generation and seeding, and digital signature generation and verification.

to
> Verify that only approved cryptographic **algorithms, modes** of operation are used for key generation and seeding, and digital signature generation and verification.
****
In a similar way, for [11.2.2](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x20-V11-Cryptography.md#v112-secure-cryptography-implementation) clarify from "ciphers and modes" to "ciphers, modes".
And change from:
> Verify that the application is designed with crypto agility such that random number, authenticated encryption, MAC, or hashing algorithms, key lengths, rounds, **ciphers or modes** can be reconfigured, upgraded, or swapped at any time, to protect against cryptographic breaks. Similarly, it must also be possible to replace keys and passwords and re-encrypt data. This will allow for seamless upgrades to post-quantum cryptography (PQC), once high-assurance implementations of approved PQC schemes or standards are widely available.

to
>
Verify that the application is designed with crypto agility such that random number, authenticated encryption, MAC, or hashing algorithms, key lengths, rounds, **ciphers, modes** can be reconfigured, upgraded, or swapped at any time, to protect against cryptographic breaks. Similarly, it must also be possible to replace keys and passwords and re-encrypt data. This will allow for seamless upgrades to post-quantum cryptography (PQC), once high-assurance implementations of approved PQC schemes or standards are widely available.

******
For [11.6.2](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x20-V11-Cryptography.md#v116-public-key-cryptography), as we have In Appendix V "Cryptography" the approved KEX Schemes described (the same as we have for approved hash functions and algorithms there), to clarify "industry-proven" -> "approved" and change from 
> Verify that **industry-proven** cryptographic algorithms are used for key exchange (such as Diffie-Hellman) with a focus on ensuring that key exchange mechanisms use secure parameters. This will prevent attacks on the key establishment process which could lead to adversary-in-the-middle attacks or cryptographic breaks.

to 
> Verify that **approved** cryptographic algorithms are used for key exchange (such as Diffie-Hellman) with a focus on ensuring that key exchange mechanisms use secure parameters. This will prevent attacks on the key establishment process which could lead to adversary-in-the-middle attacks or cryptographic breaks.
Yes, OK for me. Feedback from someone more knowledged on the topic would be welcome 😉
@oleksiidov please open a PR for now

Apologies @oleksiidov, @randomstuff, I looked more closely and I think there may have been a grammar misunderstanding which led to the "ciphers, modes" being used everywhere even where that is not grammatically correct.

https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/pull/3018/commits/ca016f1218b203f12741b65b9d0694da96cb04c2

I also added what we mean by approved.

Please respond to the comment and let me know if you have any other concerns about my changes.
